entries.title: Big Ten, SEC Support College Sports Bill After Late Trump Pressure Campaign
entries.summary: The country’s two most powerful conferences pledged support for the bill after a series of intense negotiations, clearing the way for a Senate vote before summer recess.
entries.content:
The Big Ten Conference and the Southeastern Conference, the country’s most powerful collegiate sports conferences, have backed a bipartisan college sports bill after a flurry of intense discussions.

The conferences shared their support for the Senate’s current version of the Protect College Sports Act in a joint statement Friday night, writing that they came to an agreement “following detailed and productive negotiations” with bill sponsors Ted Cruz (R-Texas), Maria Cantwell (D-Washington) and Eric Schmitt (R-Missouri).

Their endorsement is a major boost to the sweeping sports bill — and came after a series of 11th-hour meetings forced this week by lawmakers eager to kill the obstacle presented by large conferences, who had opposed the bill for months over several provisions like capping power-conference membership and salary cap enforceability.

Big Ten and SEC leadership had blown past other Congress-imposed deadlines this week, but they scrambled to hold meetings on revised bill text after President Donald Trump stated his intent to publicly condemn conference leadership for opposing the bill, Yahoo Sports reported Friday night.

Dozens of other conferences, including the Atlantic Coast Conference and the Big 12, had vocally supported the measure since it was introduced in June because it would help close the revenue gap between themselves and the country’s two biggest power conferences. However, their endorsement could waver after the bill’s latest version more than doubles what top programs can pay their players — meaning the Big Ten and SEC’s richest members can further outpace smaller conferences.

“The Big Ten Conference and Southeastern Conference support the Protect College Sports Act as currently drafted, following detailed and productive negotiations with Senators Cruz, Cantwell and Schmitt, and their respective staffs,” the short joint statement reads. “We appreciate the substantial work that has gone into this effort.”

Negotiations with the conferences ran seven to eight hours a day, Schmitt told USA Today. Consensus on how a college athlete’s brand deals would impact an institution’s revenue-sharing cap was what finally got the conferences to sign off on the bill, Schmitt said.

The proposal seemed unlikely to see any meaningful progress before the Senate begins its summer recess on Aug. 7, but Schmitt told Yahoo Sports on Friday that he expects a vote late next week.
entries.author: Angie Orellana Hernandez

entries.title: Trump Sticks by ‘Anti-Weaponization’ Fund Ahead of Blanche Confirmation Vote
entries.summary: The president stood by his controversial fund despite its jeopardization of an upcoming Senate vote for AG nominee Todd Blanche.
entries.content:
President Donald Trump indicated Saturday he would not waver on the controversial “anti-weaponization” fund that has threatened Todd Blanche’s nomination for attorney general.

Trump said on Truth Social he would “push hard” to get congressional approval for the $1.8 billion pool of money — a fund that Blanche signed off on as part of the president’s settlement against the IRS.

That approval would be nearly impossible to attain in the current environment: Critics from both sides of the aisle have raised concerns about offering payouts to people who participated in the Jan. 6 Capitol riots and other Trump allies.

Chief among the dissenters are outgoing Sens. John Cornyn (R–Texas) and Thom Tillis (R–North Carolina), who have withheld voting for Blanche until they have receive written guarantees that the Justice Department will kill the fund. Trump accused the duo of retaliating after the president refused to back their reelection campaigns earlier this year.

“It will immediately be back on the table,” Trump said of the fund, “and I will get it done.”

Trump, his two eldest sons and the Trump Organization appealed the ruling on Friday to the 11th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in hopes of blocking the ruling a federal judge made earlier this month that Trump and the Justice Department had manipulated the judicial process to benefit the president and his allies.

Trump repeated on Saturday he was willing to leave Blanche as acting attorney general until Cornyn and Tillis are out of office next year. Senate Judiciary Chair Chuck Grassley (R–Iowa) rescheduled a vote for Blanche on Tuesday, but Cornyn and Tillis have signaled they will not change their positions.

“President Trump clearly intends to resurrect the payout pot for punks either by inappropriately establishing another bogus fund or pushing Congress to vote for a bill that the majority of Republicans in the Senate would be against,” Tillis wrote on Saturday in response to Trump. “It’s unfortunate that Todd Blanche, who I consider qualified for the job, will not be confirmed because of this reversal.”
entries.author: Angie Orellana Hernandez

entries.title: Trump, Burgum Blast Pirro For Dropping Reflecting Pool Damage Case
entries.summary: The president and interior secretary criticized the U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia’s office for dropping a vandalism charge against a former Olympian.
entries.content:
President Donald Trump and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum still say vandals damaged the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, a day after federal prosecutors said government contractors — and the DOI — were to blame.

Trump criticized U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro’s motion to dismiss the case after the agency assessed that a “flawed installation by the contractor” caused damage to the famed water feature. The filing contradicted the president and other White House officials’ weekslong allegations of vandalism.

“I don’t know what she was thinking?” Trump said of Pirro, one of his staunch allies, on Truth Social Saturday. “There may have been some contractor difficulty, but the major damage was caused by VANDALS!”

Trump attached an image of a sizable imprint of the numbers “8647,” a sequence interpreted by the White House as a threat against the president, left on the National Mall’s grass. Authorities have said they were investigating the matter.

Burgum also decried Pirro’s decision not to prosecute David Hearn, a former Olympic canoeist, and others accused of vandalism. Pirro’s office cast blame on the DOI and other agencies in the court filing, saying the department had erroneously presented a grand jury with evidence of vandalism despite recently unveiled documents that proved otherwise.

Burgum maintained on Saturday that his department provided the U.S. attorney’s office with “expert and eyewitness testimony to the damage done by vandals and provided every piece of evidence they asked for in the requested time line detailing each area of damage at the pool.”

Some of the vandalism was also caught on camera, Burgum said.

“We won't back down to deranged people who want to destroy, deface, or degrade our monuments,” Burgum wrote in an X post.

Trump had ordered changes to the Reflecting Pool ahead of the Fourth of July holiday. Algae blooms appeared shortly after the nearly $15 million work was completed and blue material surfaced at the pool, likely from the coating Trump wanted to be painted “American flag blue.”

Hearn’s legal team said on Friday after his charges were dropped that the Justice Department should never have brought the case forward to begin with. They demanded a public apology.
entries.author: Angie Orellana Hernandez
